Audio description (AD), also referred to as a video description , described video , or visual description , is a form of narration used to provide information surrounding key visual elements in a media work (such as a film or television program , or theatrical performance ) for the benefit of blind and visually impaired consumers. These narrations are typically placed during natural pauses in the audio, and sometimes overlap dialogue if deemed necessary. [ 1 ] Occasionally when a film briefly has subtitled dialogue in a different language, the narrator will read out the subtitles.
